newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Troops foil anti-military march in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Troops foil anti-military march in Sierra Leone.

text.p: A massive show of force by troops in the Sierra Leone capital on Monday foiled plans by students to march against military rule, witnesses said.
Hundreds of soldiers and former rebels backing the military junta that seized power on May 25 patrolled Freetown in jeeps and on foot, while others searched motorists at roadblocks.
Troops brandishing rocket-propelled grenades and matchetes swarmed the city's Eastend district, the planned starting point of the march by the National Union of Sierra Leone students.
Other soldiers blocked off the only road leading to Freetown's Foura Bay College on a hill above the city.
Witnesses said some student leaders had been arrested while several others were in hiding.
"Nothing is going to stop us," one student leader said from hiding. "We may not come out today but maybe next week."

In the first serious internal challenge to junta leader Major Johnny Paul Koroma since the coup, the students are demanding the reinstatement of ousted elected president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who is exiled in neighbouring Guinea.
The toppling of Kabbah just over a year after he won elections ending four years of military rule has been condemned by the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.

The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has imposed a land, sea and air blockade of Sierra Leone and troops of its Nigerian-led military wing, ECOMOG, have clashed repeatedly with junta soldiers and their rebel allies.
Police citing security concerns banned the planned march and vowed to deal ruthlessly with any violations.
Tension rose sharply in the city ahead of the planned march.

The few shops that had reopened in Freetown after the pillaging that followed the coup were shut again on Monday. The Sierra Leone Commercial Bank, the only bank that obeyed orders from the military to reopen, shut its doors again on Monday.
The streets were largely empty of traffic and pedestrians, but large crowds gathered at street corners to watch the show of force by the military.
Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha, who heads ECOWAS, arrived in Abidjan on Monday for talks with Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie believed to focus on Sierra Leone.
Nigerian officials said Abacha was then heading for Guinea.
Nigeria, Ivory Coast, Guinea and Ghana are members of a special committee of the 16-nation ECOWAS dealing with the Sierra Leone crisis.
Talks between foreign ministers of the committee and envoys of the Freetown government broke down last month in Abidjan after Koroma said he would retain power until 2001.
ECOWAS ordered sanctions to be stepped up and Nigerian troops clashed last week at Freetwon airport with forces backing the military junta.
The foreign ministers ended talks in the Ghanaian capital Accra at the weekend to decide the next line of action.
